skill.name: paper-context-resolver
skill.description: Rigor Paper Context helper for README-first deep learning repo reproduction. Use only when the README and repository files leave a narrow reproduction-critical gap and the task is to resolve a specific paper detail such as dataset split, preprocessing, evaluation protocol, checkpoint mapping, or runtime assumption from primary paper sources while recording conflicts. Do not use for general paper summary, repo scanning, environment setup, command execution, title-only paper lookup, or replacing README guidance by default.
skill.summary: Resolve narrow paper details that block README-first deep learning repository reproduction.
skill.author: lllllllama

content.user_title: Resolve Paper Details for Reliable Reproduction
content.value_statement: Repository documentation can omit details that are essential for reproducing deep learning results. This skill resolves narrow gaps from primary paper sources while documenting conflicts.
actual_capabilities: Resolves specific dataset versions and split details from primary paper sources.
Identifies reproduction-relevant preprocessing and postprocessing requirements.
Clarifies evaluation protocols that repository documentation leaves ambiguous.
Maps checkpoints to model variants when source evidence supports the mapping.
Separates direct source evidence from inference and records README-paper conflicts.
limitations: Requires a concrete reproduction question and existing repository evidence.
Does not provide general paper summaries or broad related-work reviews.
Does not scan repositories, configure environments, or execute commands.
Cannot resolve details that are absent from the supplied or located primary sources.

use_cases.title: Clarify an Evaluation Split
use_cases.description: Compare the repository instructions with the linked paper to identify the exact evaluation split and document any disagreement.
use_cases.target_user: Machine learning engineer reproducing published results

use_cases.title: Verify Preprocessing Details
use_cases.description: Extract only the preprocessing details needed to complete an experiment when the README omits essential parameters.

use_cases.title: Map Checkpoints to Variants
use_cases.description: Use primary source evidence to connect available checkpoints with documented model variants without assuming unsupported mappings.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve One Missing Detail
prompt_templates.prompt: The README does not specify [missing detail]. Use [paper link] to answer only this reproduction question and distinguish evidence from inference.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one clear documentation gap and a known paper link.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Dataset Split
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the repository evidence with the primary paper for the [dataset] split. State each source's claim and record any conflict.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experiment depends on choosing the correct training or evaluation split.

prompt_templates.title: Verify an Evaluation Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve the evaluation protocol for [model and task]. Check metrics, data partition, checkpoint selection, and preprocessing using primary sources only.
prompt_templates.scenario: A researcher needs several connected details for a faithful evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an Evidence Resolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Given [repository evidence], [paper sources], and [reproduction question], produce a narrow answer with source claims, conflicts, inferences, and unresolved uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced reproduction review requires a traceable resolution across multiple primary sources.

output_examples.input: The README names the dataset but not the evaluation split. Check the linked paper.
output_examples.output: The paper evaluates on the official validation split. The README does not contradict this, but it does not state the split explicitly.

output_examples.input: Determine whether the released checkpoint matches the base or large model.
output: Direct evidence: The project page labels the checkpoint as the base variant.
Repository evidence: The filename does not identify a variant.
Resolution: Treat it as the base model and preserve the missing repository label as a documentation gap.

output_examples.input: The README and paper specify different image sizes. Which value should the reproduction report use?
output_examples.output: Record both values as a conflict. Preserve the README-first instruction for repository reproduction and note the paper value as supporting context.

best_practices: Start with one concrete reproduction-critical question after reviewing the README and repository files.
Prefer README-linked papers, official project pages, arXiv, or OpenReview primary records.
Report source disagreements explicitly and label every inference.
anti_patterns: Do not request a general summary when only one reproduction detail is missing.
Do not replace README instructions silently with values from a paper.
Do not present speculative settings as source-supported reproduction requirements.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after repository inspection reveals a narrow, reproduction-critical question that primary paper sources can answer.

faq.question: Can it summarize an entire paper?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on specific details needed for reproduction, such as splits, preprocessing, evaluation, checkpoints, or runtime assumptions.

faq.question: Which sources does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers README-linked papers, official project or paper pages, arXiv, and OpenReview primary records.

faq.question: What happens when the README and paper disagree?
faq.answer: The output records both claims, explains the conflict, and preserves the README-first policy.

faq.question: Does this skill execute repository commands?
faq.answer: No. It does not scan repositories, configure environments, or execute commands.

faq.question: Can it infer missing details?
faq.answer: It can identify limited inferences, but it labels them clearly and does not present them as direct evidence.
